Is late-follower status in AI currently an advantage — capital-allocation efficiency versus the risk that AI relocates the user interface away from the device?
Are Apple Pay and App Store commissions genuinely exposed to near-term disruption from crypto/AI payment rails, with adoption evidence and a 2-5 year timetable?

levers.domain_notes: Sourcing is primary-document-first, not literature-first: Apple 10-K/10-Q filings via SEC EDGAR, court records from US v. Google (search remedies), US v. Apple, Epic v. Apple, and European Commission DMA decisions carry more weight than any analyst note. The query explicitly rejects the sell-side product-segment frame, so commentary organised that way is background at best. FRED supplies rate and macro series for the discount-rate and duration arguments; academic sources (OpenAlex, SSRN working papers) are the right route for passive-flow and quality-factor evidence, where peer-reviewed factor literature outranks practitioner assertion. Recency window: financial figures within the last four reported quarters, legal and regulatory developments within the last 18 months, factor and market-structure literature may be older where the mechanism is stable. Disclosed and court-surfaced figures outrank estimates; where Apple does not disclose a line separately (Google TAC, App Store commissions), state the estimation method and give a range rather than a false point estimate.

rationale.register: The query asks which of the bull and bear cases the evidence actually favours and demands explicit adjudication of contested points — evaluation-shaped. It stops short of advocate because it forbids a buy/sell/hold recommendation and attaches no course of action.
rationale.inference_depth: The central question requires inference over absences: Apple deliberately does not disclose Google TAC or App Store commission revenue separately, so the durability decomposition must be reconstructed from court-surfaced discovery figures, regulatory filings and gray literature. That is the defining condition for deep.
